translations.text: Then, because he had so great a longing for Christ's coming, an answer came to him from the Holy Spirit, that he would not taste death before he had seen Christ.
God commanded his people in the old law that they should offer him every firstborn male child, or else redeem it with five shillings.
If, however, any woman were so poor that she could not obtain these things, then she was to bring two young pigeons, or two turtledoves.
If, then, we are so poor that we cannot offer the greater good to God, then we must bring him two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, that is, a twofold compunction, of fear and of love.
If, however, you will do no good to the honour of God, then by that vice you reveal your wickedness, and that wickedness will destroy you before God.
The turtledoves signify chastity: they are so made that if one of them loses the other, the living one never seeks another mate.
He who believes in him sees him now with his faith, and in the eternal life with his eyes. Simeon said further, "He is a light for the revelation of the nations, and the glory of your people Israel."
All these words Simeon spoke concerning the child to the heavenly Father, who sent him to mankind.
Just as light drives away darkness, so too the love of Christ and faith in him drive all vices and sins away from our hearts; and he is the glory and bliss of all believing people.
And also his resurrection from death, and his ascension to heaven, and all the wonders that he worked, all of them were signs, and the unbelieving spoke against them, and the believing believed.
When she saw her child taken, and iron nails driven through his hands and through his feet, and afterwards his side wounded with a spear, then Christ's suffering was her suffering;
Although Mary believed that Christ would rise from death, nevertheless her child's suffering went very sharply into her heart.
and she was dwelling within God's temple during all that time; and she then came to the child, and prophesied about him, and gave praise to God."
This Anna, of whom we are speaking, did not love delicacies, but loved fasts. She did not love idle talk, but devoted herself to her prayers.
This Anna, of whom we spoke a while ago, was a widow. Zacharias, John's father, was a married man; both he and his wife prophesied about Christ.
Those have true virginity who from childhood remain in chastity, and through God's help scorn all lust in themselves, both of mind and of body.
He grew and was strengthened in his human nature, and he needed no growth and no strengthening in his divine nature.
